raj (runtime): heads up — ran a small apples-to-apples sweep comparing synthetic loadgen vs replay harness on two stacks, results look inconsistent across GPUs. looking for quick triage before a wider run.
sara (sre): brief numbers?
raj (runtime): A100-40GB (image A) vs H100-80GB (image A, same tag) — synthetic: p95 ~ 78ms, p99 ~ 210ms. replay: p95 ~ 85ms, p99 ~ 480ms on H100 (same replay trace). that's ~2.2x worse tail. overall throughput roughly same.
mike (bench): can you paste the exact image + driver + cuda so we can reproduce?
raj (runtime): image: ghcr.io/redwood/inference:2026-03-rapid-batching-cuda12.1-rtv4
driver: NVIDIA 535.86.05
cuda: 12.1
kernel: 5.19.0-42-generic
(note: both runs used identical image tag and model checkpoint)
jen (infra): interesting — did you pin container runtime flags? cgroups, cpuset? those matter for KV caching locality.
raj (runtime): cpus/affinity were default. run used run.sh --batching-policy=adaptive --kv-mode=local --prefetch=on
sara (sre): KV cache hit rate for replay vs synthetic?
raj (runtime): synthetic KV hit ~ 91% (prefix reuse high), replay KV hit dropped to 62% on H100 run. on A100 replay hit was 88%. so H100 replay shows much worse cache behavior.
mike (bench): that smells like either kernel scheduling or driver differences causing thread preemption or different GPU SM scheduler defaults. did you compare nvidia-smi topo or MIG configs?
raj (runtime): topo identical; no MIG. both are single GPU instances. but H100 host had different BIOS power profile and a slightly newer driver minor.
jen (infra): list BIOS and nvidia-smi -q? also check container runtime (runc vs crun) and seccomp. can add to matrix.
benchbot: summary attached: {"run_id":"2165432100-1","p95_synth":78,"p99_synth":210,"p95_replay":85,"p99_replay":480,"kv_hit_synth":91,"kv_hit_replay":62} :bar_chart:
mike (bench): thanks. next hypothesis: batching window shrank under replay because tail events forced early flush (batcher timeout). do we have per-batch size/time histograms?
raj (runtime): yes — in replay H100 we saw median batch size drop from 8 -> 4 for long sequences and batch_wait_time increased jitter. synthetic keeps sizes ~7-9.
sara (sre): could kernel flags like mitigations or CPU governor be different? CPU freq scaling can affect host-side pre/post work and feeding GPU.
jen (infra): H100 host was on clouds-prod image: linux-image-5.19.0-42 with kernel cmdline: quiet splash intel_pstate=active mitigations=auto. A100 host used 5.15 with intel_pstate=passive mitigations=off.
mike (bench): that could be huge. scheduling jitter + p-states affect batching heuristics. try disabling intel_pstate or pinning cpu governor to performance for H100 run.
raj (runtime): queued a quick test: boot flag changes and re-run replay. also toggled RT_PRIORITY for runtime process. initial quick run: p99 dropped from 480 -> 260 with governor=performance, kv_hit up to 78%. small win.
sara (sre): good sign. still not matching A100. other differences? kernel modules, hugepages, CFS tunables?
jen (infra): container image diff: the H100 host had a different glibc minor, and our image was rebuilt on newer base; there's also a different glibc symbol resolution that changes small allocations timing (we've seen this before).
mike (bench): for apples-to-apples, we need matrix: GPU type, driver version, kernel version, image build-id, cpu governor, container runtime. propose a test plan:
- step 1: lock image by digest (not tag) and re-run on both GPUs
- step 2: match driver+cuda exact minor versions (if impossible, try older driver on H100)
- step 3: force cpu governor=performance + disable power governor features (thermal throttling off for test)
- step 4: run synthetic + replay back-to-back with identical seed and same loadgen concurrency
- step 5: collect: per-request latencies, batch size/time histograms, kv hit/miss timelines, trace spans for host pre/post GPU submission
please ack if you want this as a job.
raj (runtime): ack. I'll make a reproducible infra job and store artifacts in s3://redwood-bench/2165432100-parity-check. will include perf, eBPF traces for the process and gpu submission timestamps.
sara (sre): one more: add test where batching heuristic is forced to fixed-window (e.g., --batcher-fixed-size=8 --batcher-max-wait-ms=12) to see if adaptive policy interacts badly with replay jitter.
mike (bench): yes — and add kernel flag experiment: "mitigations=off" vs "mitigations=auto" and set nohz_full for runtime cpus. small matrix but high signal.
jen (infra): I'll snapshot the guest images and pin driver packages. also will run a quick micro-benchmark: tiny loop that does host memcpy+cudaLaunch to measure submission jitter.
raj (runtime): timeline: creating job today, run overnight, post results morning. quick note: observed one oddity in tracing — kernel selection for conv kernels differed between synthetic and replay for the same model on H100 (different heuristics picked based on seqlen distributions). possible cause: replay has more long tails -> runtime kernel selector falls back to alternate tiling.
mike (bench): capture the kernel name table and kernel selector decisions in traces. if selector is non-deterministic under jitter, that's actionable — we can add a deterministic override for experiments.
sara (sre): ok. try to keep runs short but enough samples: 30k requests each. we'll triage tomorrow and decide whether to roll a rollback or add fallback. :eyes:
raj (runtime): thanks. tagging @jen for infra follow up. :thumbsup:
jen (infra): got it. I'll post matrix and job links once queued.
benchbot: job queued: s3://redwood-bench/2165432100-parity-check/ artifacts will appear under run-*/
raj (runtime): closing loop here — will paste raw traces when available. if anyone sees obvious blindspots call them out now. :wave:
